paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God did the work first, and then He asked for an answer. Before Joshua says a word about choosing, the LORD walks through everything He has done. He took Abraham from beyond the Euphrates, brought Israel out of Egypt, and gave them "a land on which you did not toil" (Joshua 24:13). Everything Israel has, God handed to them, so the call to serve Him comes from a God who already showed up.

Then comes the line that gets me every time: "choose for yourselves this day whom you will serve" (Joshua 24:15). Joshua puts the choice right out in the open, and he doesn't water it down. When the people promise fast and loud, Joshua tells them, "You are not able to serve the LORD" (Joshua 24:19), and I think he wants them to feel how big this promise is. Then he tells them to "get rid of the foreign gods among you" (Joshua 24:23), and a promise with foreign gods still hiding in the corner is only half a promise.

So here's what I'd carry out of my bakery today, baker. Serving the LORD is a choice you make on purpose, and it comes with real things to put down. Joshua said it plainly: "As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD!" (Joshua 24:15). Israel served the LORD all through the days of Joshua and the elders who outlived him (Joshua 24:31).
